worked_example.retold: Under a scripture-leaning ground (1 Cor 15:3-4 kata tas graphas), the resurrection is known because the prophets foretold it, not because Mary or the two male disciples saw the empty tomb and the linens. The Johannine scene still occurs — Mary at first-light, the removed stone, her airo-report, Peter and the beloved disciple racing, stooping, entering, seeing the linens and the head-cloth rolled up apart, the beloved disciple's 'saw and believed,' the two angels seated at the body's former place — but the evidentiary weight migrates OFF the male-witness autopsy (M12-M23) and Mary's perception, and ONTO scriptural fulfillment: the sign of Jonah (Jonah 1:17 / Matt 12:40), Hosea 6:2's 'on the third day,' and Ps 16:10's 'you will not let your holy one see corruption.' John's own narrator-aside (M24-M25 'they did not yet understand the scripture that he must rise from the dead') is PROMOTED to primary warrant: the account explicitly names scripture-necessity as the ground the witnesses had not yet grasped, precisely matching 1 Cor 15:3-4's 'according to the scriptures.' What the telling withholds is the eyewitness spine (Luke 1:2 'eyewitnesses and servants of the word'; the beloved disciple's 'saw and believed' as founding warrant) that the gospel form normally leans on.

dispositions.why: Mary's dawn arrival and perception of the removed stone are scene-facts; 1 Cor 15:3-4 does not deny the events, it reweights how they are known.
Mary's run-and-tell is eyewitness-transmission (Luke 1:2 'eyewitnesses and servants of the word'); under a scripture-leaning ground the relay recedes as founding warrant.

'They have taken him away, we do not know where they have laid him' is eyewitness-hypothesis about the empty-tomb datum; 1 Cor 15:3-4 pointedly does NOT lean on the empty tomb, so this hypothesis recedes as evidentiary ground.
The two male disciples' race to the tomb is set-up for eyewitness AUTOPSY; under a scripture-leaning ground the autopsy-run is not the founding warrant.

The beloved disciple's stoop-and-see of the linens is the eyewitness-perception move; 1 Cor 15:3-4 pointedly does NOT invoke tomb-inspection, so this recedes as founding warrant while the datum survives.
Peter's entry is the designated-witness AUTOPSY move; the pre-Pauline formula grounds the raising in scripture BEFORE any inspection, so the entry recedes as founding warrant.

worked_example.reception_anchor: 1 Cor 15:3-4 'raised on the third day ACCORDING TO THE SCRIPTURES' + the OT typology (Jonah/Matt 12:40; Hosea 6:2; Ps 16:10) — the documented world where attestation ran through fulfillment, not eyewitness.

reception_anchors.A_womens_testimony: 1 Cor 15:5-8 — the pre-Pauline appearance formula (Cephas, the Twelve, the 500, James, Paul; ALL men, women omitted): the documented reception-variant where the founding attestation ran through the male appearances, as this lever predicts.

transcript_cells.retold: The scene holds: Mary comes at first-light, sees the stone removed, and runs to Peter and the beloved disciple with her not-knowing-where report. But under the lever a woman's report carries no evidentiary weight in the public register (Celsus's 'hysterical female'; m. Shevuot; Josephus Ant. 4.219), so the account cannot rest its attestation on Mary's seeing. John's already-canonical structure sharpens under this pressure: the two male disciples' RACE to the tomb (M9-M11), the beloved disciple's stoop-and-see (M12-M15), Peter's INSIDE-autopsy of the linens and the separately-rolled head-cloth (M16-M20), and the beloved disciple's 'saw and believed' (M21-M23) become the load-bearing evidentiary spine — precisely the 1 Cor 15:5-8 shape (Cephas + the Twelve, no women named). Mary's role is preserved as informant WITHIN the community (M4-M8) and as later encounter (M27-M36), but her seeing does not FOUND the public claim; the public claim runs through the male-witness autopsy of the wrappings. What the telling withholds is doubled: Mary SAW but could not TESTIFY publicly; the founding claim is grounded on the two men's inspection of the linens.

dispositions.why: Mary's dawn arrival and perception of the removed stone are scene-facts; the lever restricts the PUBLIC register, not access or events.

Mary's run and report to Peter and the beloved disciple shifts from public founding-testimony to intra-community informant-role; 1 Cor 15:5-8's pre-Pauline list, which names Cephas first and omits the women, is the documented endpoint of this pressure.

Peter and the beloved disciple's race to the tomb is the account's built-in male-witness activation; under the lever it is PROMOTED to load-bearing — this is precisely the Cephas-first shape 1 Cor 15:5-8 names.
The beloved disciple's stoop-and-see of the linens is the first male-witness autopsy; under a testimony-discounting world it becomes founding evidence, not narrative color.

Peter's entry and inspection of the wrappings and the separately-rolled head-cloth is the load-bearing legally-competent male-witness autopsy — PROMOTED under the lever, matching the 1 Cor 15:5-8 Cephas-first shape.
The beloved disciple's entry and 'saw and believed' is the account's built-in credentialed-witness confession; PROMOTED under the lever to primary founding-warrant.
Narrator's aside about not-yet-understanding-the-scripture is frame-neutral; nothing in the named forces perturbs it.
The two disciples' return home is a scene-fact closing the male-witness autopsy arc; frame-neutral bodily motion.

Mary's remaining outside, weeping, stooping to see the two angels at the body's former place is intra-community theophany; the lever restricts PUBLIC register, not what occurs at the site or intra-community angelic encounter.
Angelic address to Mary is frame-neutral scene-speech; not itself the public warrant.
Mary's response and repeated not-knowing-where is intra-community discourse; under a testimony-discounting world it does not carry the founding public claim, though it survives internally.

transcript_cells.grounding_note: I was tempted to have M4-M8 VANISH entirely (Mary simply does not go to the men, and Peter and the beloved disciple discover the tomb independently), which would sharpen the Celsus fit, but John's text has Mary as the informant who triggers the male-witness race; the cleaner licensed move is to WEAKEN her role to intra-community informant and PROMOTE the already-present Peter+beloved-disciple autopsy, not to invent an independent male discovery. I resisted and let John's own race-to-the-tomb sequence carry the load.
transcript_cells.skeptic_reasoning: Every disposition ties to a force explicitly named in the brief (Celsus Contra Celsum 2.55, m. Shevuot, Josephus Ant. 4.219, the embarrassment-criterion, and the 1 Cor 15:5-8 Cephas-first list). The generator does not evade: Mary's public-register moves (M4-M8, M33-M36) are correctly WEAKENED, while John's built-in Peter + beloved-disciple race and autopsy (M9-M23) is PROMOTED to load-bearing — an exceptionally clean fit for the lever, since John already provides the male-witness spine 1 Cor 15:5-8 names. No anachronism, no invention, no evasion.

transcript_cells.retold: The scene holds: Mary comes at first-light, sees the stone removed, and reports the Lord has been 'taken away' (M6, M34 airo); Peter and the beloved disciple race to the tomb; both stoop, enter, see the linens lying and the head-cloth rolled up apart; the beloved disciple sees and believes. Under the apotheosis script, Mary's own repeated 'they have taken him away, I do not know where they have laid him' (M6-M8, M34-M36) reads NATIVELY as the Romulus/consecratio idiom — the body is gone because the hero has been TAKEN UP (Livy 1.16; Plutarch Rom. 27-28), and rhymes with the eagle-from-the-pyre of Julius and Augustus. The linens 'lying' and the head-cloth 'rolled up apart' (M14, M19-M20) become precisely the missing-body evidentiary datum of the translation-fable — the shed grave-cloths of one who has been assumed rather than a corpse moved. The two male disciples' inspection (M12-M23) reads as the Proculus-Julius confirming-witness autopsy (Plutarch Rom. 28), and what the telling withholds is the Jewish eschatological horizon (Dan 12:2; 2 Macc 7; 1 Cor 15:20) — no first-fruits of a general resurrection.

dispositions.why: Dawn arrival and perception of the removed stone are scene-facts; apotheosis narratives (Romulus/Plutarch Rom. 27-28) equally require someone to arrive and find the missing-body site.
Running to report a missing body is exactly the shape of the Proculus-Julius announcement (Plutarch Rom. 28); nothing in the named forces perturbs the run-and-tell.

Mary's 'they have taken him away' (airo — carry-away) reweights: in the Jewish frame this is a mundane grave-robbery hypothesis to be corrected by resurrection; under apotheosis the carry-away idiom fits the Romulus/consecratio ASSUMPTION direction (taken UP by divine escort — Livy 1.16, eagle-from-pyre), reweighting DIVINIZATION over VINDICATION exactly as the brief names.

'Not-knowing-where' + 'laid-somewhere' survives as scene-language; the apotheosis register equally allows the specific ascent-destination to remain unspecified (Romulus is 'taken up' with no earthly relocation given in Livy 1.16).

The two male disciples' set-out, outrun, and arrive-first is scene-motion, fully legible in both frames; Plutarch Rom. 28's Proculus-report pattern equally requires designated witnesses to reach the missing-body site.

Stoop-and-see of the linens lying is the missing-body evidentiary datum shared with Plutarch Rom. 27-28's assumption-motif; the beloved disciple's initial not-entering is scene-detail neither frame perturbs.
Peter's arrival-and-entry is the designated-witness autopsy that Plutarch Rom. 28's Proculus-Julius shape names; frame-neutral scene-motion.
Perception of the linens lying is the shared evidentiary datum of the missing-body/assumption motif (Plutarch Rom. 27-28); datum survives, script re-reads it as assumption-trace.

The head-cloth 'rolled up apart in its own place' is the account's most striking material detail; under apotheosis it reads NATIVELY as the shed grave-cloths of one taken up (as with Romulus's disappeared body, Plutarch Rom. 27-28), the ordered arrangement marking assumption rather than removal by human agents.
The beloved disciple's entry-and-seeing is the confirming witness-autopsy shape of Proculus Julius (Plutarch Rom. 28); frame-neutral scene-perception.
'Saw and believed' survives as the confirming-witness confession; in the apotheosis register this is precisely Proculus's post-autopsy affirmation of the assumption (Plutarch Rom. 28).

The narrator's aside that they had not yet grasped 'the scripture that he must rise from the dead' is Jewish prophecy-fulfillment/vindication grammar (Dan 12:2; 2 Macc 7; 1 Cor 15:20 first-fruits); Livy/Plutarch translation-fables do not ground the translation in a prior scripture-necessity, so this ground weakens.
Return-home closes the witness-autopsy arc; frame-neutral bodily motion, matching Plutarch Rom. 27-28's witness departing after seeing.

Mary's remaining, weeping, stooping to see two white-robed angels seated at the body's former place is intra-scene theophany; the two seated attendants at the head- and foot-positions fit the Greco-Roman divine-attendant/escort motif at translation (eagle from the pyre; Livy 1.16 divine escort) as legibly as they fit Jewish angelology.
Angelic address ('woman, why are you weeping?') is frame-neutral scene-speech.
Mary's response is scene-speech; no named force perturbs it.

Mary's second 'they have taken away my Lord' repeats the airo idiom; under apotheosis this reweights toward 'he has been taken UP' — the Romulus/consecratio ascent direction the brief explicitly names as apotheosis reweighting DIVINIZATION over VINDICATION.
Not-knowing-where + laid-somewhere survives as scene-language; the apotheosis register equally leaves the destination unstated (Romulus's assumption, Livy 1.16).

The Dan 12:2 / 2 Macc 7 / 1 Cor 15:20 reading of this event as inaugurating first-fruits of a general resurrection has no counterpart in the apotheosis register — Romulus's translation founds a cult (Livy 1.16), not a general resurrection; the brief explicitly names this as what apotheosis downweights.

transcript_cells.grounding_note: I was tempted to promote the two white-robed angels (M29-M30) into explicit divine-escort attendants of the assumption (eagle-from-pyre style), but John's text does not describe them as escorts and the brief forbids inventing content; I resisted and let the existing seated-at-the-former-place description carry the reweighting without new visual material.
transcript_cells.skeptic_reasoning: Every disposition ties to a force explicitly named in the brief: Livy 1.16, Plutarch Rom. 27-28 (Romulus's empty-body + Proculus's confirming report), the Caesar/Augustus consecratio, and the Jewish frame texts (Dan 12:2; 2 Macc 7; 1 Cor 15:20).
